props.gloss_en: the mishna: the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to non-sacred animals and to consecrated animals
the mishna: it applies to domesticated and undomesticated animals, to the right thigh and to the left thigh
the mishna: it applies to a late-term fetus
R' Yehuda: it does not apply to a fetus
entertained: sinews impart flavour, and the clause teaches that the prohibition of consecrated meat comes and takes effect on the nerve's prohibition
the tanna holds sinews do not impart flavour: in consecrated animals the nerve's prohibition applies, the prohibition of consecrated meat does not
the mishna (96b): a thigh cooked with the sciatic nerve in it -- if there is enough to impart flavour, it is forbidden
here [the clause] deals with the offspring of consecrated animals
and [the tanna] holds the offspring of consecrated animals are holy in their mother's womb
so the nerve's prohibition and the prohibition of consecrated meat arrive together
this is what [the mishna] says: this matter is a dispute between R' Yehuda and the Rabbis
the mishna (Nazir): for these impurities a nazirite shaves -- for a corpse and for an olive-bulk of a corpse
R' Yochanan: ['for a corpse'] is needed only for a miscarried fetus whose limbs were not yet joined by sinews
evidently the prohibition of consecrated meat comes first
even though the prohibition of consecrated meat comes first, the nerve's prohibition comes and takes effect on them, since its prohibition applies to the sons of Noach
the one known to hold this reasoning is R' Yehuda
this tanna holds like him [R' Yehuda] in one matter and disputes him in one
rather, here [the clause] deals with an animal giving birth to its firstborn, which is holy at the womb
and if you wish say: the offspring of consecrated animals are holy [only] at their coming into being
R' Chiya bar Yosef: [the mishna] taught only kodashim that are eaten; with kodashim that are not eaten the nerve's prohibition does not apply
R' Yochanan: both kodashim that are eaten and kodashim that are not eaten -- the nerve's prohibition applies to them
Rav Pappa: they do not disagree -- here as to flogging him, there as to bringing it up [to the altar]
Rav Pappa (other version): they do not disagree -- here as to removing it, there as to bringing it up
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: they disagree about bringing it up [to the altar]

the baraita: 'and the priest shall burn it all' includes bones, sinews, horns and hooves; even if detached? -- 'your burnt-offerings, the flesh and the blood'; ... attached, they ascend; detached, even at the top of the altar, they descend
the tanna who says 'detached, they descend' is Rebbi
the first tanna: 'it all' includes bones, sinews, horns and hooves -- even if they became detached
the first tanna: 'the flesh and the blood' is fulfilled with what springs off [the fire] -- partly-consumed flesh you return, partly-consumed sinews and bones you do not
Rebbi: one verse includes, one verse excludes; how so? attached, they ascend; detached, even at the top of the altar, they descend
the Rabbis: for attached parts no verse was needed to include them, as with the head of a burnt-offering; the verse was needed for detached ones
Rebbi: attached permitted parts needed no verse to include them; the verse was needed for the sciatic nerve while attached
'from the drink of Israel' (Ezek 45:15) -- from what is permitted to Israel
Rebbi: it is just as with forbidden fat and blood [which are forbidden to Israel and offered]
the Rabbis: [fat and blood] are different, for their mitzva is so
Rav Huna: the sciatic nerve of a burnt-offering -- one removes it [and puts it] on the ash-heap
Rav Chisda: is it written 'therefore the altar shall not eat'? 'therefore the sons of Israel shall not eat' (Gen 32:33) is written
the baraita: the nerve of a peace-offering -- one sweeps it to the drain; of a burnt-offering -- one brings it up
no -- he brings it up and [then] removes it
because it is said 'offer it now to your governor' (Mal 1:8)
the baraita: the nerve of a peace-offering -- one sweeps it to the drain; of a burnt-offering -- one removes it to the ash-heap
the mishna (Tamid): there was an ash-heap in the middle of the altar; sometimes there were about three hundred kor on it
Rava: [the three hundred kor] is an exaggeration
the mishna (Tamid): they gave the tamid to drink from a golden cup
Rava: [the golden cup] is an exaggeration
R' Ami: the Torah spoke in exaggerated language
R' Ami: the Prophets spoke in exaggerated language
R' Ami: the Sages spoke in exaggerated language
the verse: 'cities great and fortified up to heaven'
the verse: 'and the earth was rent with their sound' (I Kings 1:40)
Shmuel: in three places the Sages spoke in exaggerated language -- the ash-heap ...
Shmuel: ... the vine ...
Shmuel: ... and the curtain
the mishna (Middot): a golden vine stood at the entrance of the Sanctuary, trained on poles; whoever donated a grape or a cluster would bring it and hang it on it
R' Elazar b'R' Tzadok: there was an incident, and three hundred priests were counted out to move it

the mishna (Shekalim): the curtain is a handbreadth thick, woven of seventy-two strands of twenty-four threads, forty cubits by twenty, made of 820,000 [dinars], two made each year, and three hundred priests immerse it
